content.comment_body: My [product_name] V8 is still at version [version_no]. Previously, I used [product_name] V7, which was at [version_no]. I continue to prefer the older V7, as it feels more refined and has fewer issues. Will the V8 ever get resolved, or has [company_name] abandoned this product?
[product_name] [version_no] is the most recent release. Earlier versions are no longer available from [company_name].
Curious to hear more about your observations. Personally, I favor V8 for its new features, but I'd like to know your reasons—not looking to debate, just trying to understand your perspective.

My main frustration is needing to choose the cable interface repeatedly for every new input, and manually starting the device. I also encounter errors when I run programs originally developed in V6/V7, especially with math and display blocks—though maybe those errors just surface in the new version. The interface makes calibration tasks cumbersome: loading values many times is straightforward in V7, but in V8 it's much harder and more time-consuming.

It's odd that with [article_no] and newer, the Ethernet connection must be selected for each download repeatedly. Many popup windows are too large for the screen, making it impossible to access buttons like OK or APPLY. Resizing helps temporarily, but the issue returns. The latest [product_name] still isn't available in Dutch or other languages, though English is acceptable for programming. The older versions had a Dutch HELP function. When introducing [product_name] with [article_no], the team assured Dutch support was coming, but the timeline keeps slipping.

If you work exclusively with [article_no] (and newer), there is a way to avoid repeatedly selecting the interface. On my Windows 7 system, in my user directory, there's a folder named ".[product_name][version_no]" containing "application.ini". After selecting the cable and correct COM interface, close [product_name]. Then open "application.ini" in Notepad and find 'ConfirmBeforeComm = true'. Change it to 'ConfirmBeforeComm = false' and save. This makes the cable selection permanent. To revert, just switch back to 'ConfirmBeforeComm = true'.

Here's my full .ini file: #Properties #09.11.2004 dialog.parameter.showInNewWindow=true app.height=540 pathbase=. showPropertyOnNew=true app.width=720 openSaveDir=Samples port=COM1 hardware=[product_name] udf.hardware=[product_name]UDF DE.[company_name].ad.kop.app.[product_name]KOP.grid.visibility=true DE.[company_name].ad.kop.app.[product_name]KOP.grid.distance=95 update.internet.server.url=[url] simulation.startAutomatically=true simulation.resetFlag=false I added 'ConfirmBeforeComm=false', but it didn’t help.
It’s unclear why your application.ini file has so few entries. Mine already had 'ConfirmBeforeComm = true', so I just changed it to 'false', and it worked as expected.

Looking at the first lines of your application.ini, the date shows 2004, but my file was accessed just yesterday. It's likely you edited an outdated file—there may be several similar files on your PC, and you might have chosen the wrong one.

The application.ini you modified exists within the program installation directory—which is incorrect. For reference: my username is [user_name]. The file you edited is in the system folder, but the correct file is in my user profile directory, ".[product_name][version_no]".

Found the correct file here: C:\Documents and Settings\all\.[product_name][version_no]. Thanks for the workaround! However, I still have to manually start the device after programming, so I plan to use V7 until improvements are made. Doesn’t seem like [company_name] supports the product anymore. The jump from V7 to V8 was major, but no updates yet—have the programmers been reassigned or let go? For comparison, I've used Microchip's MP LAB since 1996 and it receives updates frequently.

To be honest, the likelihood of your hopes being realized is low. [company_name] tends to be slow about fixing known bugs or making requested improvements in updates. It's rumored that the developers follow this forum, but if so, they don't seem interested in resolving existing issues.
A new question about exporting bin files from [product_name] V8 has been posted by [user_name] in a separate thread. Best regards, [user_name]

Thanks for the workaround! I'll try it soon. What about the issue where FBD blocks don't line up properly? Sometimes, blocks snap incorrectly to the grid, even though they're identical, and aligning them is tedious. Also, split connections behave oddly if they're close to another block—the end jumps many pixels instead of moving smoothly. When further away, you get precise control. I uploaded an example, not sure if it's machine-specific. Never saw this in V7. Strange we're still using V8.0.0 from 2014.

[product_name] is available in Dutch via a local file, not through online updates. Download the Dutch language file from the website and run the update locally, making sure to run [product_name] as Administrator. Update 3: I found the website to download the Dutch file.
A new question about updating from [version_no] to [version_no] using a luf file was posted by [user_name] in a separate thread. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience noticeable usability setbacks and persistent bugs after moving from V7 to V8.0.0 of [product_name]. Major concerns include having to repeatedly select connection interfaces, inefficient calibration workflows, incomplete language support, errors when importing older projects, and large dialog windows hiding controls. Compared to previous versions, the latest release is seen as less refined and more prone to issues, leading to frustration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a smoother workflow with fewer repetitive steps, reliable compatibility with older project files, proper localization (especially Dutch and other languages), and a user-friendly interface that fits standard screen sizes.
